after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,2),(-1,2),(-1,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(1,-1)$
- $(0,-2)$
- $(-2,-1)$
after.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{{90}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-2,0),(-2,-1),(0,-1).$

So, the correct answer is "III only."

after.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of ${i,j}$ under $A$, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =A(i)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i \\ {j}^{′} & =A(j)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14094357/assets/4e0e5c9cee037bded1f5739af35c3a8acfaa4d4e6f469b3e50afe69b96990e39.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\pi $ radians (counterclockwise or clockwise) about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $Av$, we need to rotate $v$ (counterclockwise or clockwise) by an angle of $\pi $ radians, as shown below.
